sections.heading: The suvat equations for constant acceleration

questions.q: A car starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at $2.5$ m/s$^2$ for $8$ seconds. Find its final velocity and the distance traveled, using $v=u+at$ and $s=ut+\dfrac{1}{2}at^2$.
A ball is thrown upward with initial velocity $u=15$ m/s. Using $g=9.8$ m/s$^2$ (deceleration), find the maximum height reached, using $v^2=u^2+2as$ with $v=0$ at the top.
A cyclist decelerates uniformly from $12$ m/s to rest over a distance of $36$ meters. Find the deceleration, using $v^2=u^2+2as$.

A particle accelerates uniformly from $u=2$ m/s to $v=14$ m/s over $6$ seconds, then travels at constant velocity for a further $4$ seconds. The velocity-time graph is shown. Find the total distance traveled, using the area under the graph.
questions.answer: Distance in first phase (trapezoid): $\dfrac{1}{2}(2+14)(6)=48$ m. Distance in second phase (rectangle): $14\times4=56$ m. Total: $48+56=104$ m.

questions.q: A particle decelerates uniformly from $v=20$ m/s to rest over $5$ seconds, giving a velocity-time graph that is a straight line from $(0,20)$ to $(5,0)$. Find the distance traveled, using the area under the graph.
questions.answer: The graph forms a right triangle with base $5$ and height $20$. Distance $=\dfrac{1}{2}(5)(20)=50$ m.

questions.q: A stone is dropped from a height of $45$ meters. Using $g=9.8$ m/s$^2$, find the time taken to reach the ground, and its speed on impact.
A ball is thrown vertically upward with initial speed $u=24.5$ m/s. Using $g=9.8$ m/s$^2$, find the total time taken to return to its starting point.
questions.answer: Time to reach the highest point: $t=\dfrac{u}{g}=\dfrac{24.5}{9.8}=2.5$ s. By symmetry, the total time to return to the starting point is $2\times2.5=5$ s.

A particle has velocity $v=4t-t^2$ (m/s). Find its displacement from $t=0$ to $t=2$, and its acceleration at $t=2$.

sections.heading: Finding when a particle is at rest or changes direction

questions.q: A particle has velocity $v=t^2-5t+6$ (m/s). Find the times at which the particle is instantaneously at rest.
A particle has velocity $v=t^2-7t+10$ (m/s). Find the times at which the particle is instantaneously at rest.
Two cars start 300 meters apart on a straight road and travel toward each other, one at $18$ m/s and the other at $12$ m/s, both at constant speed. Find the time until they meet.
questions.answer: Combined closing speed: $18+12=30$ m/s. Time $=\dfrac{300}{30}=10$ seconds.

questions.q: Two cars start at the same point on a straight road, one traveling at $25$ m/s. The second car starts 4 seconds later, traveling at $30$ m/s. Find how long after the first car starts the second car catches up.
questions.answer: Let $t$ be the time (seconds) after the first car starts. First car's position: $25t$. Second car's position (starting 4 s later): $30(t-4)$. Setting equal: $25t=30(t-4)=30t-120$, so $5t=120$, giving $t=24$ seconds.

sections.heading: A well-designed word problem: a train between two stations

questions.q: This question has two parts. A train starts from rest at station A and accelerates uniformly at $0.5$ m/s$^2$ until it reaches a speed of $20$ m/s. It then travels at this constant speed before decelerating uniformly at $1$ m/s$^2$ to come to rest at station B. The total distance between the stations is $2400$ meters. (a) Find the time and distance covered during the acceleration phase. (b) Find the total journey time between the two stations.
questions.answer: (a) Acceleration phase: $t_1=\dfrac{v-u}{a}=\dfrac{20}{0.5}=40$ s. Distance: $s_1=\dfrac{1}{2}(0+20)(40)=400$ m. (b) Deceleration phase: $t_3=\dfrac{20}{1}=20$ s, distance $s_3=\dfrac{1}{2}(20+0)(20)=200$ m. Constant-speed distance: $2400-400-200=1800$ m, taking $t_2=\dfrac{1800}{20}=90$ s. Total journey time: $40+90+20=150$ seconds.
